result.scope: This is the error rate of the whole map. If part of the map was predicted from other inputs, that part's rate can differ widely from it. On a PASTIS map with half its tiles read without the optical input by a probe trained on radar plus optical, that half's rate was 74.1% against 19.7% on the rest, while random samples of 300 estimated 46.9% on average. Read by a probe trained on radar alone, that half was still 28.3% wrong against 19.7% (exp88). Draw the sample with --condition to get each part's rate.

forbidden_claims.why: alpha=0.1 was fixed for this call; the guarantee holds only for an alpha fixed before the labels were seen. Proposing or evaluating another alpha after seeing these bounds (e.g. that a looser alpha would certify some share of the map) is not a certification: another alpha tests other levels, a level whose upper_bound is below an alpha is not thereby accepted, and trying alphas until one certifies is not covered

the rule ('prefix' here) is fixed with alpha before the labels are seen; re-running certification under another rule after this one certified nothing is a second look that the guarantee does not cover; prefix accepts levels from the smallest zone upward while p_value <= delta = 0.1 and stops at the first failure (the smallest zone's p_value is 0.139); bonferroni accepts any level with p_value <= delta/19 = 0.00526 (the smallest p_value of the 19 levels tested is 0.0222), so no level passes under either rule

a random design makes a certified zone possible, never certain: olmoearth_certify_zone certifies a zone only where the labels drawn in it hold few enough errors for its exact test, so it may certify none, and no design, sample size, budget or plan can promise a certified (or 'certifiable') region, or a zone of any size; this random design of 300 labels certified nothing at alpha=0.1, and a new one with a larger budget may certify nothing either

the whole-map error rate describes the whole map, not its most confident part: set against alpha=0.1 it neither explains nor predicts that no zone certified, and it does not show that every part of the map is above alpha; the evidence on the most confident part is the smallest zone tested, coverage 0.1: 33 labels, 1 wrong

levels_tested.how_the_rule_tests_them: prefix tests the 19 levels at delta = 0.1 each, from the smallest zone up, stopping at the first whose p_value is above it; the levels after that one are not accepted (bonferroni would test each of the 19 levels at delta/19 = 0.1/19 = 0.00526316)

result.design_note: Strata are the map's classes (Olofsson et al. 2014): each class gets at least 50 labels, or all its windows if it has fewer, and the rest of the budget goes to the classes in proportion to their size. This budget is for a random sample's interval, not this class design's: olmoearth_estimate_map_error reports first the interval valid at every sample size, then the design's union bound over the classes, which the package says is wider than a random sample's interval when the classes' error rates are close and can be narrower when they are far apart; if only the whole-map rate is needed, design='random' can give a narrower interval.
